builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis
summary: Agent4Spec replaces manual, one-time authoring and maintenance of OpenAPI specifications with a two-pipeline multi-agent system that self-corrects syntax errors and proposes market-driven endpoint additions. It costs multiple coordinated LLM calls per specification, which is feasible on third-party APIs with no local GPU requirement, but adds orchestration complexity and per-document token spend compared with a single lint-and-review pass. It can fail when the validation loop accepts plausible but semantically wrong corrections, and the market-analysis pipeline can generate endpoint suggestions based on unreliable competitive research that engineers must still review, since roughly half of suggestions were not adopted.
rationale: The method runs entirely on hosted LLM APIs and addresses a bounded task (OpenAPI validation and gap analysis), so a small team maintaining API specifications can pilot it cheaply, but its value depends on verifying correction accuracy and suggestion adoption on their own specifications before production reliance.
technique: Multi-agent API specification validation and market analysis

claims.statement: Agent4Spec replaces manual, one-time authoring and maintenance of OpenAPI specifications with a two-pipeline multi-agent system that self-corrects syntax errors and proposes market-driven endpoint additions. It costs multiple coordinated LLM calls per specification, which is feasible on third-party APIs with no local GPU requirement, but adds orchestration complexity and per-document token spend compared with a single lint-and-review pass. It can fail when the validation loop accepts plausible but semantically wrong corrections, and the market-analysis pipeline can generate endpoint suggestions based on unreliable competitive research that engineers must still review, since roughly half of suggestions were not adopted.

Top-performing LLM achieves 100% syntax error detection, over 95% implementation success for proposed corrections, and over 50% adoption rates for suggested endpoint improvements among 9 evaluated models.
